note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Remember, other: The remember line says thinking, memory, language and problem solving 'keep growing' from infancy to old age. The card only says development continues and that learning 'can' extend it. Memory and processing speed often decline in old age, so this overstates the card and could mislead students.

rejected.title: Intellectual development
card: Intellectual development is growth in the ability to think, remember, use language and solve problems. It is about the mind, not changes in the body or in managing feelings.
It begins in infancy, when babies learn by sensing and handling the world. Children then gain language and learn to reason.
Thinking becomes more abstract in youth, so young people can weigh ideas, plan ahead and consider other points of view.
Intellectual development continues through adulthood and old age. Learning new skills, work and study can all extend it.
rejected.remember: Thinking, memory, language and problem solving keep growing from infancy to old age.

opts: A child learns to use new words to explain a problem
A child grows 6 cm taller over one year
A child makes a close friend at school
A child learns to calm down after losing a game
a.why: Using new words to explain a problem shows growth in language and problem solving, which are intellectual. Growing taller is a change in the body, and making friends and calming down are about relating to others and managing feelings.
a.clue: Look for the change in thinking or language.

b.q: Sam, aged 68, joins a class to learn Italian and now plans a trip using what he has learned. What does this show?
opts: Intellectual development continuing in old age
Physical development as his body adjusts to ageing
Emotional development as he learns to manage feelings
Memory use alone, with no growth in language or thinking
b.why: Learning a new language and planning a trip use memory, language and problem solving, so Sam is still developing intellectually in old age. It is tempting to see this as just remembering words, but he is gaining a new language and using it to plan, which is growth in thinking.
b.clue: Which skills is Sam using to learn and to plan?
